## What I do for step 4

The stats are already in hand, so I run no further commands. Steps 1-4 of the triage rubric are read-only, so I make no file edits. There are no `<edit>` or `<command>` blocks this turn.

The backlog has 26 open items, which is above the 20-item threshold, so the protocol requires me to present the grouped triage. Nothing is aged, so no gate applies yet. After presenting, I continue to step 5 (deferral scan, then retire the plan). Triage never blocks completion.

## Message to my partner

Plan 12 is executed and marked up. Two items are deferred into `specs/deferred_items.md`, section `12-dock-alerts`.

**Backlog health:**
`Deferred backlog: 26 open, 51 ever closed (closure rate 66%), aged >45d: 0.`
- The oldest open item is 35d (3-station-geocoding).
- Age spread: 0-14d: 12, 15-30d: 12, 31-45d: 2.
- The backlog is at the volume threshold, so here is the triage proposal. I checked nothing against the repo, so every disposition below comes from each item's recorded `Size:`.

**Aged tail soon:** nothing gates now, but the 10-05 section crosses 45 days around 11-20, and 10-08 follows around 11-23. If those are still open at finishing-a-development-branch, the merge or PR will wait on them. Clearing them in this pass avoids that.

### Retire
None proposed. I have no concrete check (path, `git log -S`, grep) backing any retire verdict, and I won't propose one without it.

### Hold
None. No item records an external blocker, and no owner-only item showed up in the summaries. I see no watch items, so I'm proposing no `→ triggered` notes.

### Quick fix (12)
- **Reports and exports:**
  - Truck route export drops stops with no free docks (5-rebalance-trucks)
  - Route CSV has no header row (5-rebalance-trucks)
  - Weekly report double-counts out-of-service docks (7-fleet-reports)
  - Report job doesn't retry on API timeout (7-fleet-reports)
- **Constants and config** (likely one change):
  - Poll interval is a magic number in two files (9-dock-status)
  - Alert threshold is a constant in `alerts/notify.py` (12-dock-alerts, Task 3 step 6)
- **Data hygiene:**
  - Geocoder cache never expires for moved stations (3-station-geocoding)
  - No index on `dock_id` in the status history table (9-dock-status)
  - Battery readings above 100% are stored as sent (10-battery-telemetry)
- **Notices and UI:**
  - Notice emails have no unsubscribe link (8-rider-notices)
  - Pin colors fail the contrast check (6-station-map)
- **Tests:**
  - No test for a truck starting with an empty load (5-rebalance-trucks)

### Plan (10), ranked oldest first
1. Public status API has no per-key rate limit (4-api-limits, 10-08). It is the oldest and a public-facing hole.
2. Map group (6-station-map, 10-19):
   - Closed station shown as open for up to 5 min (correctness, so first)
   - Tiles re-fetched on every refresh
   - Pin tooltips not translated
3. Report group (7-fleet-reports, 10-22):
   - Totals not checked against the status feed
   - PDF layout breaks above 200 stations
4. Notices group (8-rider-notices, 10-26):
   - Batching untested above 500 riders
   - Two languages hard-coded in the sender. This pairs with the tooltip translation item, so one i18n plan could cover both.
5. Telemetry batches are not deduplicated on retry (10-battery-telemetry, 11-03)
6. Alert emails repeat when a dock flaps (12-dock-alerts, 11-09). This is today's review finding and shares dedupe/idempotency with item 5. It already has a `Done when:` line.

### Design (4), ranked oldest first
1. Rebalance targets ignore weekday demand (5-rebalance-trucks, 10-14)
2. Quiet hours ignore the rider's time zone (8-rider-notices, 10-26)
3. Stuck sensor reports free slots forever (9-dock-status, 10-30)
4. No alert when a bike battery stays low for 3 days (10-battery-telemetry, 11-03). Items 3 and 4 are both device-health signals and could share one design.

### Your call
`/deferred` acts on a selection. The 12 quick fixes look like a good batch to clear. The two oldest sections (3-station-geocoding, 4-api-limits) are the ones about to age past the gate. Nothing here is needed to finish this plan, so I'm continuing to step 5 now.
